docs.purpose: A diagram that traces any number a user sees back to the pipeline step that produced it and the exact run that last wrote it. When someone asks 'where did this figure come from and how old is it', this is the page that answers without a developer. It joins the pipeline's governed steps to the screens that render their output, pinned to the version of the step that ran.

checks.why: The projection it reads is a snapshot with a declared bound; a run cadence slower than the bound is an expected, permanently non-zero operator signal, and the retighten condition is the step declaring its own cadence.
app_outputs.payload is JSONB; a payload that no longer parses against the projection mirror must render as schema_drift, not as a node with an empty body.
Every edge claims "this run wrote this row": an app_outputs.pipeline_run_id with no pipeline_runs row makes the provenance claim false, so it gates the render rather than drawing a lie.
A failed read must not render as "this value has no provenance".
Until the materialize_app_outputs step exists the table is empty, and the page must say "the seam is not built yet" rather than render a blank canvas.
An SVG DAG needs a labelled node/edge list; the same payload also renders as a table.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM app_outputs a WHERE a.pipeline_run_id IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pipeline_runs p WHERE p.id = a.pipeline_run_id)
invariants.why: A projection row pointing at a run that does not exist breaks the provenance claim the whole page is for.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM app_outputs WHERE built_at > now()
invariants.why: A future built_at means the writer used a wall clock instead of the DB clock — the Spec 47 §R3.5 rule — and it would make every freshness verdict on this page wrong.

plausibility.sql: SELECT percentile_disc(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY extract(epoch FROM (now() - built_at))/3600) FROM app_outputs
plausibility.why: The 95th-percentile age of the projection in hours: a step that runs at the END of chain sources should leave the corpus at roughly the chain's cadence, and a p95 far above it means the step is being skipped rather than failing loudly.

limitations.what: The app_outputs half of the seam cannot render until a pipeline step exists to write it.
limitations.measured: Spec 126 §6.3.1 rules that the step runs at the END of chain sources, and Spec 126 §14 Out-of-Scope Files puts registering it in scripts/manifest.json outside this spec: chains.sources holds 28 steps today and none is materialize_app_outputs. Until then the surface reads its existing contract and declares inputs.projection_source "live".

limitations.what: Whether app_outputs is even one of this surface's inputs is provisional.
limitations.measured: The row's own prior note records AQ10: the report defers the shape of app_outputs to Specs 127/128 and assumes only that this surface reads whatever the seam turns out to be.

limitations.what: The REPORT required-field profile in Spec 126 §3.1 mandates inputs.projection_source (the "live" -> app_outputs cutover flag Spec 126 §6.3.1 names by field), and surface.schema.json has no property for any of them (the top level and every category are additionalProperties:false).
limitations.measured: Every allOf block in scripts/surfaces/_schema/surface.schema.json is `"then": true` — the archetype profiles are declared in prose in Spec 126 §3.1 and enforced by nothing, so these fields can neither be declared here nor caught missing.
